articles.title: Why is gasoline suddenly under $4 a gallon?

articles.title: Greetings from Senegal, where breakdancers are competing in the Youth Olympics

articles.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to a prisoner exchange as talks end with no big breakthrough

articles.author: Willem Marx
articles.description: Iran-backed operatives have been charged over nearly 20 attacks, including a plot on a U.K. base housing U.S. troops. Separately, a U.S. soldier is held in the U.K. on Russia spying claims.

articles.description: Rep. Kevin Kiley, a former Republican turned independent, lost his reelection bid. He discusses what went wrong for the GOP, the challenges of the two-party system and how Congress could work better.

articles.author: Hettie O'Brien
articles.description:
In today’s newsletter: US intelligence reportedly believes the former tech executive was recruited by Beijing, raising questions about the security of the AI industry and Trump’s close ties to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang

Good morning. Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang, the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies.
Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. That’s after the headlines.
UK | Ministers are considering changing the law to force the entertainment industry to better protect women and children in the wake of the revelations over David Walliams and the conviction of Russell Brand.
Climate | The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country.
US midterms | Democrat Scott Colom has become the first Black senator in Mississippi to be elected since Reconstruction, in a stunning upset after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states.
Europe | Millions of people across Spain have joined the country’s first general strike in 14 years, setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power.
Technology | Police officers risk arresting innocent people, especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thursday briefing: What we do (and don’t) know about Alice Huang and the Nvidia affair

articles.author: Jonathan Yerushalmy
articles.description:
This live blog is now paused – but you can read the latest report on Nvidia and Jensen Huang’s future as CEO here
Too big – and too well-connected – to sack? 
Huang does not enjoy the supercharged voting rights that are par for the course elsewhere – his shareholding is a plain vanilla 3.6%. On the other hand, Nvidia’s board does not appear to have spent much time worrying about succession planning and “key person risk” or other standard concerns of corporate governance wonks outside the US.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nvidia board reportedly meeting to decide CEO Jensen Huang’s future as chip giant’s share price plunges – follow live

articles.author: Dara Kerr and agencies
articles.description:
The meeting comes after the executive and co-founder admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy
Nvidia’s board of directors met on Wednesday to decide whether to oust Jensen Huang as CEO of the world’s most valuable chip company, according to multiple reports, after a tumultuous week in which the executive and co-founder of the company admitted to having a romantic relationship with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy.
The meeting marks ⁠a sharp shift from Sunday, when Nvidia’s board ​expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team, and the company’s stock slid more than 8% in after-hours trading after the Wall Street Journal reported that ⁠the company was preparing to fire Huang.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nvidia board reportedly deciding whether to oust CEO Jensen Huang as stock price plunges

articles.author: Caitlin Cassidy and Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
‘You just don’t mess or play with a 400-tonne train’, Sydney Trains says as 17-year-old suffers multiple injuries to head, chest and pelvis

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A 17-year-old boy is in a critical condition after falling from the outside of a train on the Sydney Harbour Bridge while he was likely train surfing, NSW police say.
Around 11.30am on Thursday, emergency services were called to the railway corridor between Wynyard and Milsons Point train stations following reports someone had fallen from a northbound Tangara train onto the tracks on the bridge.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Teenager in critical condition after likely ‘train surfing’ on Sydney Harbour Bridge, police say

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Former police officer questioned about Instagram message he asked friend to send to Jessie Baird referencing ‘cancerous tumour’ 

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon has claimed in court that he was diagnosed with cancer by a naturopath and has been questioned about a post-breakup message to Jesse Baird where he referred to the diagnosis.
But Lamarre-Condon on Thursday told the court he could not name the naturopath or the location of their practice, claiming there had been new developments and stores had been “cleared out”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon says he was diagnosed with cancer by naturopath but doesn’t recall which one, trial hears

articles.author: Robert Mackey (now); Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
articles.description:
Colom beat Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith after race was called eight days after midterm election day

Democrat Scott Colom wins race for US Senate in Mississippi

How Colom won deep-red Mississippi with little help from Democrats

Sign up for the US Breaking News email

Some Democrats, out of the 11 who missed the key procedural vote on Tuesday to impeach Pete Hegseth, blamed a traffic jam in Washington DC for their inability to make it to the US Capitol in time.
By a vote of 211-204, Republicans referred the articles of impeachment to the judiciary committee – effectively killing the effort to oust Hegseth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Scott Colom claims victory as he addresses supporters in Mississippi following his historic Senate victory – as it happened

articles.author: Maya Yang
articles.description:
SS United States, which set transatlantic speed record during maiden voyage in 1952, is sunk off coast of Destin
The historic SS United States has reached the end of its journey at sea, sinking Wednesday off the coast of Destin, Florida, where it will begin a new life underwater as an artificial reef.
The nearly 1,000ft American-made vessel, once the fastest ocean liner in the world, was launched in 1952 and made history by setting a transatlantic speed record during its maiden voyage. The ship carried thousands of passengers across the Atlantic over 17 years of operation before being retired in 1969.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Historic US ocean liner sinks near Florida to become world’s largest artificial reef

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo
articles.description:
Since the US war on Iran began in February, there have been hundreds of oil spills, posing a ‘generational’ threat to wildlife
The vast, dark slicks in the strait of Hormuz are visible from space. Throughout October, oil tankers were struck by missiles or sea mines in the waterway and spilled crude into the sea. The pollution has spread across the Gulf, contaminating coastlines and threatening to cause lasting damage to marine ecosystems that are home to dolphins, sea turtles and countless species of fish.
Eight months into the war between the US and Iran, one of the world’s busiest oil shipping routes has become a battlefield and the centre of a growing environmental disaster.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Oil slicks seen from space: the devastating impact of boat strikes on fragile Gulf ecosystems

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
William, 17, was reported missing after straying from his camp near Walhalla in Victoria’s Gippsland region

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A teenager has shared an emotional reunion with his mother after being found alive following almost a week lost in dense bushland.
Police AirWing found William, 17, whose surname has not been shared, laying down in a creek near Walhalla, 185km east of Melbourne, in Victoria’s east on Thursday morning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘He is never leaving the house again’: mother reunites with son missing for six days in Victorian bushland

articles.author: Guardian staff and agency
articles.description:
Four critical in hospital as firefighters dig through rubble in Flatbush after building next to construction site collapses
Firefighters dug through the rubble of a three-story building in Brooklyn on Wednesday after it collapsed at the edge of a construction site, killing at least two people and trapping others beneath the wreckage.
Firefighters were called to the scene in the borough’s Flatbush section at about 4pm. News helicopter footage showed dozens of firefighters scouring the debris, with a group homing in on one area and appearing to use a saw to cut through the wreckage.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brooklyn building collapse kills at least two people and traps others in wreckage

articles.author: Achol Arok
articles.description:
Police called to Lane Cove North on Wednesday after sofa found containing human torso believed to be that of adult man

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

New South Wales police have entered their second day searching for human remains after a human torso was found in bushland on Sydney’s lower north shore.
Police were called to Lane Cove North about 2.30pm on Wednesday after receiving “a number of reports from members of the public” regarding a strong odour in the area, Supt Paul Devaney told media on Thursday morning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Human torso found in sofa in Sydney bushland prompts homicide investigation

articles.author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Former barrister who helped legally establish that secondhand smoke causes lung cancer argues states could seek up to $50bn in compensation

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian state governments could sue tobacco companies for billions in public hospital and healthcare costs, under a proposal developed by a former barrister who helped legally establish that secondhand smoke causes lung cancer.
The South Australian government is formally seeking advice on the proposal, while other states are reviewing it.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australian states could sue tobacco companies for billions in healthcare costs under proposal

articles.author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
articles.description:
Once thought to have been looted by Scottish tribes, the gilded limb is the centrepiece of a new exhibition on Roman Scotland in Edinburgh
A large bronze leg found in a bog in rural Scotland more than 200 years ago and then hidden away in a duke’s storeroom is helping to rewrite the history of the Roman empire.
Antiquarians argued that the so-called Mislington leg had been looted, perhaps from York, hacked off by marauding Scottish tribes and carried north over Hadrian’s Wall. “We cannot visualise the conditions which would have led to its erection anywhere north of the Great Wall,” said one scholar, James Curle, in 1932.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bronze leg found in Scottish bog sheds new light on Roman occupation

articles.author: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent
articles.description:
Inspectors find some officers acted on potential matches from retrospective searches without making enough checks
Police officers risk arresting innocent people, especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found.
Although the technology can help fight crime, the report found it is beset by errors and biases, and operators do not always realise they must make further inquiries to verify the data.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Facial recognition errors put ethnic minorities at risk of wrongful arrest, police watchdog warns

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Remains believed to have belonged to Africans or Afro-Brazilians repatriated after being flown back by diplomats 
Two skulls, including that of a man believed to have taken part in Brazil’s greatest slave revolt but whose remains were taken to the United States and used in racist eugenics studies at Harvard University, were repatriated on Wednesday.
The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century. One was taken about 190 years ago from Salvador, the capital of the state of Bahia; the other, about 160 years ago, from Rio de Janeiro – and were welcomed back in moving, subdued ceremonies in both cities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two skulls likely belonging to enslaved people returned to Brazil after Harvard used them in eugenics studies

articles.author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya and Damien Gayle in London
articles.description:
Exclusive: Madeleine Alessandri, chair of the joint intelligence committee, will take on the role of advising No 10 on climate-related national security risks
The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country.
Prime minister Andy Burnham will announce the move on Thursday at Cop31, the UN climate summit, with the new role designed to advise the government on national security risks from the climate crisis before they spell catastrophe.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK appoints world’s first special representative for climate security

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Retailer’s management to seek two-week extension of legal protection from creditors in high court
MPs have accused the owner of Poundland of extracting millions of pounds from the budget retailer when it was on a “knife-edge” as it seeks extra time to secure a rescue deal.
The management of Poundland, which employs 12,000 people and operates 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, will seek a two-week extension of legal protection from creditors from the high court on Thursday morning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Poundland owner extracted millions when chain was on ‘knife-edge’, MPs say

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Paralympian Richard Whitehead ‘gobsmacked’ at Tory leader’s speech over proposed £36bn welfare cuts
The double amputee marathon runner Richard Whitehead has criticised Kemi Badenoch for “weaponising his sporting success” to justify her proposed £36bn welfare cuts.
The Conservative leader used the example of “double amputees running marathons” in a speech this week to explain the reasoning behind her proposed cuts to disability benefits, which she said were enabling people to “live a life of dependency”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Double amputee marathon runner criticises Badenoch for ‘weaponising his success’

articles.author: Facundo Iglesia and agencies
articles.description:
Leonardo Bertulazzi, 74, awaiting extradition to Italy, reportedly used harness to flee custody
A 74-year-old former member of Italy’s radical Marxist group the Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina, the country’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday, after he reportedly hid his ankle monitor inside a tube of pork and lowered himself from a fifth-floor balcony.
Authorities placed Leonardo Bertulazzi under house arrest in Buenos Aires in 2024, prior to his extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence. He had received the sentence in 1987 for joining a subversive association and belonging to an armed group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ex-member of radical Marxist group scales balcony, escapes house arrest in Argentina

articles.author: Oliver Milman, Fiona Harvey and Graham Readfearn in Antalya, and Ajit Niranjan
articles.description:
Marshall Islands president warns of worsening floods as UN chief calls for a windfall tax on oil and gas firms
Failure to provide an overwhelming response to the climate crisis means “the world we know is over”, the president of the embattled Marshall Islands has warned, as dozens of leaders gathered in Turkey for the Cop31 climate summit.
Hilda Heine, one of a handful of Pacific Island leaders to make an impassioned speech at Cop31 on Wednesday, told other heads of state that overshooting the 1.5C Paris temperature target would mean waves eating away their shores and floods that destroy towns, schools and hospitals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The world we know is over’ without urgent climate action, leaders tell Cop31

articles.author: Ashifa Kassam in Madrid and Stephen Burgen in Barcelona
articles.description:
Twenty-four-hour stoppage draws high participation weeks before election in which far right could gain power
Millions of people across Spain have joined the country’s first general strike in 14 years, setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power.
At the centre of Wednesday’s nationwide 24-hour stoppage, singularly called for by tenants’ associations and later backed by workers’ unions, is a pushback against Spain’s deepening housing crisis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Millions join Spain’s first general strike in 14 years in protest at housing costs

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Regime adviser says Tehran could be forced into pre-emptive strikes if stalemate continues
Senior Iranian officials believe the US is planning either further military strikes or an ever-tightening economic stranglehold that will push Tehran into retaliatory action.
The assessment comes from Mehdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump planning new military assault or tighter sanctions, say Iranian officials

articles.author: Pjotr Sauer
articles.description:
US envoys to visit Moscow and Dublin on Thursday for talks with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy respectively
Russia and Ukraine have agreed to the “largest prisoner exchange” of the war at their first US-brokered talks since February but made little progress towards a broader peace agreement.
Both sides sent senior delegations to the two-day talks, led by Donald Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, in an effort to find a solution to end the nearly-five-year war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi bring progress on prisoners but not on peace

articles.description:
This blog is now closed
Separately, I am also keeping an eye on Italy, with reports that several schools are being evacuated after receiving bomb threats by emails.
According to Rai and Sky TG24, the email was signed by “Mikhail Andropov” – the same name used in several hoax bomb alarms against European flights last week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US envoys to meet Putin and Zelenskyy separately - as it happened

articles.author: Daniel Boffey in Hamburg
articles.description:
Lawyer says Britain wrong to believe in historic doctrine that crown has sovereignty over parts of oceans
Britain should not be permitted to act as a 17th-century colonial power treating the waters around the Falkland Islands as a Dominium maris Britannici, Argentina has told an international tribunal.
Marcelo Kohen, representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked Britain for apparently believing in the historic doctrine that the British crown has sovereignty over expansive parts of the oceans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Argentinian lawyer mocks UK’s sovereignty claim in Falklands oil case

articles.author: Katherine Butler, associate editor, Europe
articles.description:
Far-right populists remain insurgent and pro-EU governments are braced for Trump’s betrayal. But the midterms also showed that democracy can fight back
• Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here


“Is Maga dead?” asked Margaret, a Guardian reader in Switzerland, in a live Q&A with our correspondents after the seismic US midterm elections. If Margaret’s query expressed a hope that the Democrats’ blue wave could transform Europe’s fortunes after two years of Maga-induced trauma, she was probably not alone.
The resounding defeat for Donald Trump’s Republicans and the installation of a Democratic-controlled US Congress has been met with understandable relief in European capitals. In the short term however, the worst for Europe is not over. Trump didn’t need congressional approval, after all, to unleash a trade war on his supposed European allies, threaten to invade Greenland, try to stitch up Ukraine or go to war with Iran, an act that has inflated fuel and food prices disastrously.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is the US blue wave a turning point for Europe, too?

articles.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
articles.description:
Tomás Beltrán was shot dead amid gang warfare that has turned Latin American country into one of its most violent
Tomás Beltrán was manoeuvring his car into his garage on Sunday night when the Ecuadorian journalist was shot dead.
Beltrán ran a Facebook page with news about Calceta, a small city in the province of Manabí, whose Pacific coastline has made it a key flashpoint in the gang warfare over drug trafficking routes that has transformed one of Latin America’s safest countries into one of its most violent.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Killing of journalist underscores deteriorating conditions in Ecuador

articles.author: Deepa Parent
articles.description:
Rights groups condemn reported punishment of Kenyan migrant worker as an ‘act of violence’
A Kenyan mother in Saudi Arabia has reportedly been sentenced to 100 lashes after giving birth outside marriage.
Under the Saudi sharia law system, sex outside marriage is a criminal offence. But it is women who are disproportionately targeted, say rights groups, which have condemned the punishment as an “act of violence”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Woman in Saudi Arabia sentenced to 100 lashes for giving birth outside marriage

articles.author: Staff and agencies
articles.description:
Bessent, driving force behind US push to cripple Iran’s economy, relocates over alleged threat to his life
The US Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, has relocated from his home in the Washington area to a military base after an Iranian threat against his life, the New York Times has reported.
Bessent has spearheaded a US push to cripple Iran’s economy since the start of the Middle East war, vowing “economic asphyxiation” of the Islamic republic through a web of sanctions.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US Treasury chief Scott Bessent is reportedly latest Trump official to move to military base

articles.author: Kate Lamb
articles.description:
Capture of man from Java follows reports that hundreds are being recruited from the south-east Asian country as Moscow seeks to boost its war effort
Ukraine says it has captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war, amid what it says is a spike in recruitment by Russia from the south-east Asian nation.
The 49-year-old man from Java was taken to Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region to take part in a Russian assault, but managed to reach Ukrainian-held territory after the group came under drone attack, according to Ukraine’s state-run I Want to Live project. He was then captured by the Ukrainians.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukraine captures first Indonesian prisoner of war amid surge in Russian recruitment

articles.author: Kaamil Ahmed
articles.description:
Charities warn of lack of protection amid health fears for more than 940,000 displaced people living in flood-prone areas
Tens of thousands of Palestinians have been left in waterlogged and damaged tents after deadly storms at the weekend, while 150,000 new shelters are held outside Gaza awaiting Israeli approval to enter, aid agencies have said.
At least four Palestinian children and woman were killed as heavy rains and wind battered fragile, leaky tents. Thousands have been left without shelter and sanitation infrastructure has been destroyed, with sewage spewing into people’s tents.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thousands without shelter face lethal conditions in storm-hit Gaza as they wait for 150,000 tents

articles.author: Daniel Boffey in Hamburg
articles.description:
Countries clash over Sea Lion project as Hamburg tribunal risks deepening sovereignty dispute
The people of the Falkland Islands face “devastating consequences” if Argentina is successful in blocking development of its offshore oilfield, the attorney general for England and Wales has told an international tribunal.
Ellie Reeves, representing the British government at a hearing of the international tribunal for the law of the sea (Itlos), said billions of pounds vital to the future of the British overseas territory would be lost.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Falkland Islanders face ‘devastating consequences’ if Argentina blocks oil project, says UK

articles.author: Associated Press at the Rafah crossing
articles.description:
Seven-time F1 world champion tours border area and logistics warehouses operated by Egyptian Red Crescent
Lewis Hamilton has visited Egypt’s Rafah border crossing with the Gaza Strip to meet organisations sending humanitarian aid to the territory.
The seven-time Formula One world champion has spoken out about conflict and humanitarian crises in the region, and has called for peace. He has frequently posted on social media about children killed in Israeli airstrikes in Gaza and called for a ceasefire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lewis Hamilton visits Egypt’s Rafah crossing and Gaza aid facilities

articles.author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya and Rebecca Bailey
articles.description:
Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’

Cop31 live – latest updates

China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels, and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.
As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Former prime minister faces death penalty upon return after being sentenced in absentia over deaths in 2024 uprising
Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister applied for a new passport this week.
Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She crossed the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh from exile

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
From the assassinations of her husband and mother-in-law to press stonewalling under Modi, Belonging offers an insider’s account of India’s political evolution
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Few love stories have been as closely entwined with a nation’s history as that of Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi. The former’s much-awaited political memoir, Belonging, offers a strikingly candid account of her journey from a small town in Italy to the highest echelons of power in India – all for love, she says.
The veteran Congress party leader has been fiercely protective of her personal world. In Belonging, she opens up for the first time about the extraordinary twists and turns of a life that has largely unfolded in full public view. (The Guardian’s Hannah Ellis-Petersen has a rare in-person interview with Gandhi, and you can read an excerpt from the book here.)
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Grenades, grief and a deepening political divide: five takeaways from Sonia Gandhi’s new memoir

articles.author: Marina Dunbar and Robert Mackey
articles.description:
CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing
Nvidia said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”.
The New York Times reported in ​October that Donald Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence that Huang ‌had a close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo
Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Collision of two trains in Egypt kills at least seven

articles.author: Chris Osuh Community affairs correspondent
articles.description:
See My World, an event highlighting the pan-African thought via film, poetry and dance, builds on momentum sparked by local activists and creatives
African philosophies including exploring how lessons from the past can shape the present and near future have inspired a film festival coming to Manchester.
See My World, a day dedicated to independent creators from across the African diaspora in the north of England, will take place at the Contact theatre on 21 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How African philosophies inspired a new approach to staging film festivals in Manchester

articles.author: Rebecca Ratcliffe, Gloria Dickie and Elisângela Mendonça
articles.description:
Mumbai facility is part of Reliance Industries, owner of world’s biggest oil refinery and funder of controversial mega-zoo
The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will host its forthcoming annual awards ceremony at a venue owned by the billionaire Ambani family conglomerate, drawing criticism from conservationists over their fossil fuel businesses and their foundation’s controversial mega-zoo.
A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which awards £1m to five winners every year to invest in conservation work, confirmed to the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay that this year’s ceremony will be held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on 17 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Environmentalists criticise choice of Earthshot prize venue owned by fossil fuel firm

articles.author: Amy Hawkins
articles.description:
Activists fear Bangkok will give in to pressure from Beijing despite reports of torture and human rights abuses against the mostly muslim ethnic minority
The deportation of two more Uyghurs to China from Thailand would put their lives in grave danger, activists have said, with one of the men saying he would be “like a slave” if he was sent back.
Last year, Thai authorities forcibly deported 40 Uyghur men to China despite pleas from the men themselves and the UN.
 

 

 The US and Canada had reportedly offered to resettle them, but Bangkok appeared to want to avoid upsetting Beijing. The UN has said the returnees’ whereabouts remain unknown.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Uyghurs facing deportation by Thailand say they will be ‘like slaves’ in China

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families
The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.
The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result
The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.
Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
A previously unseen family archive offers a glimpse into the Indian Nobel prize winner’s artistic process and personal relationships in his final years
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
It’s easy to run out of words to describe Rabindranath Tagore. The first non-European to win the Nobel prize in literature, Tagore was a Bengali poet, musician, novelist, philosopher, songwriter, painter, humanist and educator.
Born in 1861, Tagore left an indelible mark on the subcontinent’s literature, music, education and art. Among his enduring legacies are the national anthems of India and Bangladesh.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The private creative world of Rabindranath Tagore, the man Yeats called ‘greater than any of us’

articles.author: Patrick Greenfield, Elisângela Mendonça and Phoebe Weston and Spoorthy Raman
articles.description:
Guardian and Mongabay reveal approaches to officials and MPs on behalf of  Vantara zoo ahead of UK-chaired Cites meeting on endangered animal imports

British government ministers were told not to engage formally with Vantara, the controversial mega-zoo run by the Indian billionaire Anant Ambani, after lobbying efforts by the private animal sanctuary in the run-up to a UK-chaired meeting on the trade in endangered species, according to documents.
This week, the UK heads a 32-country committee meeting in Geneva of Cites, the United Nations body that regulates trade in endangered species. The meeting will examine how India has responded to compliance concerns about imports of endangered animals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK ministers told not to engage formally with Indian mega-zoo after lobbying

articles.author: Adria R Walker in Mississippi
articles.description:
Colom takes victory by razor-thin margin in state that has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982
Democrat Scott Colom defeated Cindy Hyde-Smith, the incumbent Republican senator, to become the first Black senator in Mississippi elected since Reconstruction, in a stunning upset after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states.
“All I did was have the courage to imagine a night like this,” Colom told a crowd of hundreds who on Wednesday had gathered at Tougaloo College for his victory party. “I had the courage to believe in Mississippi. I had the courage to understand that we can show the country that Mississippi matters.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrat Scott Colom unseats Cindy Hyde-Smith in stunning Mississippi Senate win

articles.author: Alexandra Villarreal in New York
articles.description:
Members of Congress seek to ‘bring sanity’ to system but decline to give details on plans to reform or abolish agency
A group of congressional Democrats on Wednesday pushed for immediate efforts to rein in the Trump administration’s sweeping immigration enforcement operation and “bring sanity” to an immigration system that Donald Trump said, after his party’s midterm drubbing, had been “too tough” in certain aspects.
Just over a week after the midterm elections in which the US president’s harsh crackdown on immigration fueled a voter backlash against Republicans, some sitting and newly elected Democrats gathered outside the US Capitol in Washington to advocate for a bipartisan approach to reforms – even as they gear up to take control of both legislative chambers next year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrats push to rein in Trump on immigration after voter backlash to ICE raids

articles.author: Adria R Walker
articles.description:
Democrat chatted up people at hair salons, colleges and at Trump rallies to become Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction
The ad is simple, less than half a minute long, but many say it was the moment the nation took notice of Mississippi’s US Senate race.
In it, the incumbent Republican senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, a cattle farmer, answers a reporter’s question about the rising price of beef: “You know, you have so many proteins to choose from,” she says.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Scott Colom won deep-red Mississippi with little help from Democrats

articles.author: Ariana Baio and Shrai Popat in Washington
articles.description:
Eleven Democrats missed the key procedural vote on the impeachment effort, which failed by just seven votes

US politics live – latest updates

Democratic lawmakers expressed outrage at nearly a dozen of their colleagues for missing a vote Tuesday evening to impeach the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, allowing Republicans to defeat the effort.
Eleven Democrats missed the key procedural vote on the impeachment effort, which failed by just seven votes. Some blamed traffic and conflicting events and others accused Speaker Mike Johnson of closing the vote early. Many of those not in the Capitol said they support the effort to impeach Hegseth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democrats lambast absent peers after Republicans block Hegseth impeachment attempt

articles.author: Claire Wang
articles.description:
Voters in Providence, Rhode Island, chose to pull foreign investments from countries that profit from genocide
The tectonic blue wave that washed over the country in last week’s midterms also brought about a historic night for the pro-Palestine movement.
Up and down the ballot, candidates who demanded an end to Israel’s war in Gaza resoundingly defeated opponents funded by the pro-Israel lobbying group American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How a small, newly socialist US city became the second to vote to cut ties with Israel

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
Republicans know that the president’s folly and excesses cost them the elections. That doesn’t mean they’re ready to challenge him
Shortly after polls closed last Tuesday, with the scale of the Republican trouncing in the midterms still becoming apparent, Donald Trump briefly adopted an oddly conciliatory tone. He declared that he was “absolutely” willing to accept the results, would look forward to working with Democrats and that deportation policies might have been “too tough”.
It was never going to last. He soon cast doubt on the elections’ legitimacy. On Friday, he replaced his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, with her deputy, Stephen Miller – a white nationalist, or “stone-cold racist”, in the words of Hakeem Jeffries, likely to be the next House speaker. Ms Wiles executed the president’s decisions faithfully, but was seen as a somewhat calming if not restraining influence, which may help explain her departure.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on Maga after the midterms: doubling down on Trumpism | Editorial

articles.author: Emma Brockes
articles.description:
He has survived blame for the US midterms disaster and dodged an impeachment vote, but it will be one battle after another now – and he can’t win them all
Like the brief, wondrous cycle of the mayfly, we may come to look back on the career of Pete Hegseth, the US secretary of defence who cheekily rebranded himself secretary of war, as the defining appointment of the Trump era: that is, one in which extraordinary power was handed to a man of cartoonish inappropriateness and which, despite this week’s shelved attempt to impeach him, may still turn out to have been luminously short-lived. In January, the Democrats will assume a majority in both chambers and are likely to have another crack at impeaching Hegseth. In the meantime, we can only look on and wonder at his meaning.
It is quite something, in the context of Trump cabinet appointments that have included Robert F Kennedy Jr and Kristi Noem, to be the most glaringly underqualified person in the West Wing, but since being sworn in almost two years ago, Hegseth has comfortably seen off any rivals to his crown. This week, eight articles of impeachment, or “high crimes and misdemeanours” as the official rubric has it, were levied against him by Thomas Massie, an outgoing Republican congressman from Kentucky, who accused Hegseth of illegal acts including violating the constitution by conducting an unauthorised war with Iran and effecting regime change in Venezuela.
Emma Brockes is a Guardian columnist
Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why does Pete Hegseth call himself secretary of war? ‘Dopey but dangerous’ wouldn’t fit on a badge | Emma Brockes

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Trump has already made history as the only president to be impeached twice. After the Republicans’ thrashing in the midterms, could there be a third attempt?
The days are getting shorter, the nights are getting longer and some Republicans are getting nervous. After a long stretch of impunity, it’s impeachment season in the US. While the attempt to impeach the defence secretary, Pete Hegseth, failed yesterday, Donald Trump may be worried he’s next.
In January, the president warned Republicans that they had better win the November elections or he would be in big trouble. “If we don’t win the midterms … they’ll find a reason to impeach me,” Trump said. He repeated this plea to voters during an October rally in Oklahoma: “Pretend I’m running, please. Just pretend. ’Cause I am on the ballot. And if we don’t win, they’ll end up impeaching me.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: It’s impeachment season! After the attempt on Pete Hegseth, will Donald Trump be next? | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Sam Levine
articles.description:
But, says one expert, it would be misleading to say that gerrymandering did not work at all in this election
If there was one obvious conclusion from Democrats’ sweeping victories in the mid-term elections on Tuesday, it seemed to be that the Republican effort to redraw congressional districts in their favor backfired.
Starting last summer, Trump and Republican allies undertook an aggressive effort to redraw congressional districts, reconfiguring the lines to give Republican candidates an advantage. Ahead of the midterms, Republicans redrew 15 seats to their advantage. After Tuesday’s election, they appear poised to lose all but two of them. “It was definitely the wrong move,” an unnamed House Republican told Fox News. “One of the truisms in politics is never to overreach. We did and that was part of the reason for the backlash.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Republican efforts to redraw congressional maps ‘failed epically’

articles.author: Amy Qin and Flávio Pessoa
articles.description:
Hundreds of datasets and websites that contradict government’s ideology have been altered or wiped – a tactic taken straight from Heritage Foundation’s policy blueprint
Even amid Donald Trump’s failures – the Iran war, soaring prices and a sharp rebuke in the midterm elections last week – there’s still at least one area his administration continues to carry out adeptly: its mass public information censorship campaign.
In less than two years, the Trump administration has done staggering damage to US data and information infrastructure. Hundreds of federal datasets have been terminated or altered, and thousands of government webpages that address diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI), the climate crisis and other issues have been quietly revised or completely wiped.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Project 2025 had a plan to target federal data. The Trump administration obeyed

articles.author: Rafael Behr
articles.description:
A lesson from the US midterms is that electorates are repelled by the arrogant mega-rich buying democracy. This is a fight Labour can afford to pick 
For most people, $224m (£168m) is a lot of money, especially if you spend it and get nothing in return. But Elon Musk is richer than most people. In fact, there is no one richer.
As the wealthiest of the US’s tech oligarchs Musk could afford to blow huge sums on a failed bid to prop up Republican candidates in Texas, his adoptive home state, in last week’s midterm congressional elections. He is reported to have spent a further $250m failing to engineer results in other races.
Rafael Behr is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: For Trump, Musk and Farage, the message is the same: voters don’t want to be hijacked by billionaires | Rafael Behr

articles.description:
Republicans in the US House of Representatives banded together on Tuesday, 10 November, to derail an effort to impeach defense secretary Pete Hegseth. The chamber voted 211 to 204 in favor of a motion to refer the impeachment charges to the Republican-led House judiciary committee, effectively stopping the effort to impeach Hegseth sponsored by Kentucky Republican representative Thomas Massie

House Republicans block effort to impeach Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth

 Continue reading...
articles.title: US House votes to derail impeachment of Pete Hegseth – video

articles.description:
New York senator Chuck Schumer expressed confidence that he would become the majority leader after the Democratic party gained at least 54 seats in the Senate during the midterm elections. Schumer's remarks came after Vermont senator Bernie Sanders announced he would not support Schumer for the leadership position. Sanders joins a growing list of Democratic senators who have said they will not support Schumer
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Schumer confident on Senate leadership role despite dwindling votes – video

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
Defense secretary calls impeachment effort a ‘farce’ and praises president in press conference for audience of one
There was no talk of “weirdos or beardos” – two among several categories whom Pete Hegseth has made it known are unwelcome in the US armed forces under his watch.
But a man with a beard had to be uppermost in his mind for him to meet journalists in the Pentagon at the ungodly hour of 8am on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hegseth lays it on thick for Trump to stave off fallout from Iran war

articles.description:
Pete Hegseth said moves to impeach him over alleged abuse of power in the Iran war were 'a farce' that would fail. The US defence secretary was speaking a day after Thomas Massie, Kentucky's Republican representative, introduced eight articles of impeachment against him


US politics: latest updates

 Continue reading...
articles.title: 'It's a farce': Pete Hegseth dismisses impeachment effort against him – video

articles.author: Martin Pengelly
articles.description:
The veteran journalist’s Crossing the Rubicon comes after a historic election where Democrats took over state legislatures across the US
Mark Danner’s new book, Crossing the Rubicon, collects his writing on politics for the New York Review of Books over the quarter-century since Bush v Gore in 2000. It arrives in the aftermath of another momentous election, the midterms tsunami that swamped Donald Trump and his Republican party and will give Democrats control of Congress next year.
From January, battle will commence between Congress and a lame duck president. Democrats have two years to hold the president accountable and build a case to take back the White House and to address damage done by the depredations of Elon Musk and Doge, by budget chief Russell Vought, and by other destructive forces.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The path is very difficult’: Mark Danner on why Democrats shouldn’t aim to only rebuild post-midterms

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright with Moustafa Bayoumi . Produced by Suzanne Gaber and Monica Espitia, engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
In an interview this week, Donald Trump was asked to give his assessment of why Republicans lost so badly in the midterms. Along with gas prices, the president blamed 'a dislike for Israel' among voters. It’s an acknowledgment that might not be made by some senior figures in the Democratic party. For years, there have been calls for them to change their stance on Israel, and now those calls are coming from newly elected members in the House and Senate. Kai Wright speaks to Moustafa Bayoumi about why the fight over Israel in the Democratic party is just beginning, and what an influx of lawmakers winning on pro-Palestine platforms means for the future of Aipac


There is a showdown looming in the Democratic party over support for Israel

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries have an Israel problem – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Imogen West-Knights
articles.description:
In 2022 and 2023, Hartshead Moor East, near Leeds, was voted the worst in Great Britain. Ever since, staff have been on a mission to redeem its reputation

The crime issue of the Long Read magazine is out now. Click here to order

In October 2023, at a service station on the M1 north-east of Leeds, Janine Gray received some bad news. She was surrounded by journalists and leading lights from the transport industry: people from the AA, the RAC, motorway service area chief executives, officials from National Highways. The big dogs. And it was among these gathered dignitaries that Gray heard the news she had been hoping, for the previous 12 months, not to hear. For the second year running, Hartshead Moor East – one half of the motorway services near Leeds that she managed – had been officially declared the worst service station in Britain.
This poll, conducted annually by the consumer watchdog Transport Focus, always makes the news. It produces gags on Have I Got News For You, punning headlines in the papers, “and finally” segments on local TV channels. Now Gray and her staff would be subjected to another round of ridicule. Of all the country’s service stations, which have a sort of aura of shitness to them anyway, theirs was apparently the shittest. Again.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We can’t be at the bottom indefinitely’: Can Britain’s most maligned service station be turned around?

articles.author: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent
articles.description:
Inspectors find some officers acted on potential matches from retrospective searches without making enough checks
Police officers risk arresting innocent people, especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found.
Although the technology can help fight crime, the report found it is beset by errors and biases, and operators do not always realise they must make further inquiries to verify the data.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Facial recognition errors put ethnic minorities at risk of wrongful arrest, police watchdog warns

articles.author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
articles.description:
Once thought to have been looted by Scottish tribes, the gilded limb is the centrepiece of a new exhibition on Roman Scotland in Edinburgh
A large bronze leg found in a bog in rural Scotland more than 200 years ago and then hidden away in a duke’s storeroom is helping to rewrite the history of the Roman empire.
Antiquarians argued that the so-called Mislington leg had been looted, perhaps from York, hacked off by marauding Scottish tribes and carried north over Hadrian’s Wall. “We cannot visualise the conditions which would have led to its erection anywhere north of the Great Wall,” said one scholar, James Curle, in 1932.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bronze leg found in Scottish bog sheds new light on Roman occupation

articles.author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya and Damien Gayle in London
articles.description:
Exclusive: Madeleine Alessandri, chair of the joint intelligence committee, will take on the role of advising No 10 on climate-related national security risks
The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country.
Prime minister Andy Burnham will announce the move on Thursday at Cop31, the UN climate summit, with the new role designed to advise the government on national security risks from the climate crisis before they spell catastrophe.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK appoints world’s first special representative for climate security

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Retailer’s management to seek two-week extension of legal protection from creditors in high court
MPs have accused the owner of Poundland of extracting millions of pounds from the budget retailer when it was on a “knife-edge” as it seeks extra time to secure a rescue deal.
The management of Poundland, which employs 12,000 people and operates 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, will seek a two-week extension of legal protection from creditors from the high court on Thursday morning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Poundland owner extracted millions when chain was on ‘knife-edge’, MPs say

articles.author: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Paralympian Richard Whitehead ‘gobsmacked’ at Tory leader’s speech over proposed £36bn welfare cuts
The double amputee marathon runner Richard Whitehead has criticised Kemi Badenoch for “weaponising his sporting success” to justify her proposed £36bn welfare cuts.
The Conservative leader used the example of “double amputees running marathons” in a speech this week to explain the reasoning behind her proposed cuts to disability benefits, which she said were enabling people to “live a life of dependency”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Double amputee marathon runner criticises Badenoch for ‘weaponising his success’

articles.author: David Batty and agency
articles.description:
L/Cpl Nicholas Horne, from 4th Battalion of Royal Regiment of Scotland, charged with one count of rape on 23 October
A British soldier has been charged with the alleged rape of a UK army servicewoman in Cyprus.
L/Cpl Nicholas Horne, who serves in the 4th Battalion of the Royal Regiment of Scotland, also known as The Highlanders, was charged with one count of rape on 23 October, the Defence Serious Crime Command (DSCC) said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British soldier charged with rape of army servicewoman in Cyprus

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
PM wrote to transport commissioner to oppose ‘megashed’ in Astley shortly before he entered No 10
Andy Burnham raised safety concerns about dozens of lorries leaving a “monster” warehouse near a primary school because there was “no safe crossing” for children, a public inquiry has heard.
Concerns about the 18-metre-high “megashed” in the village of Astley, Greater Manchester, are being examined by Britain’s office of the transport commissioner.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham raised safety concerns about Manchester ‘monster’ warehouse, inquiry hears

articles.author: Lauren Almeida and Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Broadcaster plans to make £30m in ‘temporary’ savings before inquiry into takeover by Sky
ITV plans to slash its programming budget as new figures showed that spend on the production of films and prestige TV shows in the UK was down more than £2bn over the last year.
The broadcaster plans to make £30m in “temporary” savings, including £25m in content and £5m elsewhere in the business.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ITV to cut show budgets as UK TV and film production spend drops by more than £2bn

articles.author: Denis Campbell and Tobi Thomas
articles.description:
Action on 25 and 26 November suspended to allow for formal negotations with the government
Senior hospital doctors in England have called off the 48-hour strike they intended to hold later this month after the health secretary agreed to negotiations about their grievances.
NHS chiefs, who were worried about how hospitals would cope during the action, welcomed the decision by consultants to “pause” their walkout, which was scheduled for 25 and 26 November.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Consultant doctors in England call off two-day pay strike

articles.author: Severin Carrell and Angela Giuffrida
articles.description:
Police assure parents and teachers there is no danger as thousands of schools in Italy and hundreds in the UK affected
Hundreds of schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland were hit by a fresh wave of hoax bomb threats on Wednesday, with some sites evacuated as a precaution.
Police in Scotland said that about 1,000 schools, from Dumfries in the south of Scotland to Aberdeenshire and Orkney in the north, had received the hoax warnings. At least 300 schools were affected in Northern Ireland. Similar claims were sent in a “generic communication” to schools in the Republic of Ireland.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hoax bomb threats made to schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland and Italy

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Equalities minister accuses Tories of ‘chasing Reform into the gutter’ as they drop support for planned law to ban conversion practices
Kemi Badenoch has “no interest in supporting LGBT+ people” or promoting tolerance more widely, a government minister has said, after the Conservatives dropped support for a planned law to ban conversion practices.
The comments by Bridget Phillipson, the equalities minister, come after the Tories removed their previous backing for a law targeting abusive practices that aim to change someone’s sexual orientation or gender identity.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bridget Phillipson: Kemi Badenoch has ‘no interest in supporting LGBT+ people’

articles.author: Peter Walker, Jessica Elgot, Pippa Crerar and Haroon Siddique
articles.description:
Culture secretary Lisa Nandy expected to meet leaders from TV, film and publishing and could legislate if voluntary action is deemed insufficient
Ministers have given the entertainment industry an ultimatum to bring in better protections for women and children or face government action after the allegations about David Walliams and the conviction of Russell Brand.
The culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, is expected to meet industry leaders next week, taking in representatives from TV, film, publishing and potentially sport.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: TV industry must tackle abuse or face crackdown, ministers warn

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
articles.description:
Departure of Tom Waterhouse, Reform’s ‘latest fall guy’, will be blow to party amid push towards professionalisation
Reform UK’s general secretary has left the role as Nigel Farage’s party continues to face turmoil over questions about vetting failures and professionalisation.
The departure of Tom Waterhouse comes after Reform UK’s leader on Hampshire county council, George Madgwick, was charged with 12 counts of rape and one of distributing indecent images of a child.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Senior Reform UK official quits as questions over vetting failures continue

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Keir Starmer’s former chief of staff also says the ‘thicket of rules’ about how PMs operate should be cleared away
Keir Starmer’s former chief of staff, Morgan McSweeney, has called for a rethink of “quasi-judicial” powers given to cabinet ministers such as the energy secretary’s ability to approve future oil and gas fields.
McSweeney, who helped propel Starmer to power and served as his chief of staff until February this year, said he believed “quasi-judicial processes” were stopping wider cabinet discussions and input from the prime minister on issues of national importance.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Morgan McSweeney calls for rethink of UK cabinet ministers’ ‘quasi-judicial’ powers

articles.author: Kiran StaceyPolicy editor
articles.description:
Exclusive: Cutting 2030 goal would be a ‘step backwards’, say MPs, as ministers clash over proposed reductions
Labour MPs are urging the government not to weaken its electric vehicle targets as divided cabinet ministers prepare for a crunch meeting on Thursday to thrash out a compromise.
Members of the climate and nature crisis caucus (CNCC) say ministers must not water down a legal requirement for carmakers to ensure that 80% of the vehicles they sell in 2030 are electric, saying doing so would be a backward step and “shortsighted”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Labour MPs warn against weakening electric vehicle targets ahead of crunch talks

articles.author: Ian Sample Science editor
articles.description:
Combining body mass index with other measurements and tests would lead to better care and outcomes, experts say
An alternative to BMI for diagnosing obesity could prevent misdiagnosis in millions of people worldwide, according to doctors who found it more accurately distinguished healthy people from those with harmful excess body fat.
Medical experts have long considered body mass index a blunt instrument for defining obesity, leading to concerns that substantial numbers of people with excess body fat are missed while others who are healthy are wrongly diagnosed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: BMI alternative for identifying obesity ‘could prevent misdiagnosis in millions’

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
Nats chief says he ‘quite enjoyed’ ignoring calls from Ryanair CEO to quit over system outages in September
The boss of Nats has said he was “the most disliked person in the UK” after air traffic control systems failed twice in September, disrupting flights for hundreds of thousands of passengers.
He told an aviation industry conference: “My name is Martin Rolfe, I’m the CEO of Nats – or as I like to think of myself, the most disliked person in the UK in September.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Air traffic control boss says he was ‘most disliked person in the UK’ after flight chaos

articles.author: Zoe Wood
articles.description:
Pump prices stay stubbornly high as leading bank official warns energy costs are likely to remain ‘elevated’
The price of diesel on UK forecourts remains stubbornly close to October’s record high of £2 despite a sharp fall in oil prices.
A litre costs an average of 197p, according to the AA, which described the situation as “dismal”. By contrast, petrol has fallen 6p to 168p from the peak of 174.7p in early October. That was the highest level since August 2022.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Diesel still costing close to a ‘dismal’ £2 a litre despite oil price falls

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Manufacturer says ‘shift to new energy vehicles is happening faster than expected’ and market is harsh

The Japanese carmaker Nissan has said it has been caught out by accelerating sales of electric and hybrid cars in China amid a brutal price war in the world’s biggest automotive market.
The manufacturer slashed its sales forecasts for China and said it would cut back on petrol car manufacturing while increasing production of battery electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids, which combine a smaller battery with a petrol engine.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nissan reduces petrol car production as EV sales boom in China

articles.author: Maeve McClenaghan and Rachael Healy
articles.description:
Multiple women have described unwanted sexual advances from the comedy star, allegations he denies
David Walliams, one of Britain’s best-known television personalities and top-selling children’s authors, has been accused of using his power and celebrity status to prey on young women and teenagers for sex.
The allegations, which span many years, were made in a joint investigation with ITV News into Walliams’ conduct towards young women.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What is David Walliams accused of and what has he said in response?

articles.author: Pippa Neill Environment reporter
articles.description:
Increased risk of devastating strain means restrictions imposed for second year in a row on those keeping birds
Poultry and captive birds across England and Scotland must be kept inside for the second year in a row due to an increased risk of a devastating strain of bird flu.
The British government has issued an England-wide avian influenza prevention zone, meaning individuals with 50 or more poultry or captive birds must house them inside. A similar designation was made across the whole of Scotland on Tuesday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bird flu fears prompt orders for farmers to keep poultry inside in England and Scotland

articles.author: Sandra Laville
articles.description:
181GW of gas-fired capacity proposed for sites in US and Europe because of delays in connecting to national grids, says report
Developers of AI datacentres plan to build on-site climate-destroying gas power stations on a huge scale to meet their energy demands, research reveals.
Datacentres planned across the US, the UK and mainland Europe have proposals to build fossil fuel plants on-site to create 181GW of gas-fired capacity because of delays to connect to national grids, according to the findings. This is almost four times the total peak electricity demand of Great Britain.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI datacentres plan on-site power stations on huge scale despite climate risks, research reveals

articles.author: Donna Ferguson
articles.description:
TV presenter says he was ‘genuinely unaware’ of pair’s conduct despite joking about Walliams going home with 15-year-old girl in 2004

Read the full investigation: ‘It wasn’t long until he asked me if I’d ever had sex before’

Explainer: the key legal issues surrounding the case

The TV presenter Jonathan Ross has said he is “as horrified by the revelations about David Walliams and the crimes of Russell Brand as the rest of the nation”, adding that he was “genuinely unaware of their conduct” despite making a joke about a 15-year-old “going home” with Walliams at the British Comedy Awards in 2004.
Walliams, one of Britain’s best-known television personalities and top-selling children’s authors, has been accused by several women of using his power and celebrity status to prey on young women and teenagers for sex.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jonathan Ross ‘horrified’ by David Walliams and Russell Brand revelations

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:

articles.author: Lana Crowe
articles.description:
As Hollywood begins to adopt the technology, the professionals in most direct jeopardy are the illustrators mapping out directors’ first visions. They sketch out what could be lost
A film industry dominated by AI is a dystopian prospect: stories and dialogue generated by large language models, populated by reincarnated screen icons and uncanny humanoids. That is in the future, but the real-world impact of AI is already directly affecting jobs behind the scenes, as Hollywood’s biggest film-makers begin to adopt the technology. James Cameron – long an advocate for emerging technologies in film-making – is on the board of a gen AI firm, citing his interest in how AI will intersect with CGI; Steven Soderbergh used Meta-powered tech to create animations for his recent documentary about John Lennon; even Christopher Nolan, while dismissing the idea that AI will replace humans as “nonsense”, conceded that it will create some useful “imaging tools”.
The current canary in the coalmine however is the storyboard artist, whose work gen AI appears to have directly in its sights. Storyboard artists are the illustrators who draw the panels of images with notes and diagrams that map out scenes before they are filmed. Storyboards are used to work out how a film will look, and as a blueprint to communicate a director’s vision to cast and crew, and are one of the first steps in bringing a script off the page. Now they appear on the verge of replacement by programmes that use text prompts to create illustrations instead. Even an old-school diehard like Martin Scorsese has got on board; in June he announced a partnership with an AI firm whose text-to-image model he used in the storyboarding process for his next movie.

One doesn’t have to be overly cynical to think Jensen Huang, the Nvidia boss, starts with one huge advantage as the chipmaker’s board starts its independent investigation into the alleged honeytrap spy scandal. The world of US big tech is not, to put it mildly, strong on checks and balances on a founder’s power.
Huang does not enjoy the supercharged voting rights that are par for the course elsewhere – his shareholding is a plain vanilla 3.6%. On the other hand, Nvidia’s board does not appear to have spent much time worrying about succession planning and “key person risk” or other standard concerns of corporate governance wonks outside the US.

Ever since it crashed on to PC and consoles in the late 90s, GTA has been tearing up the game-making rulebook. We explore how its cultural references, rebel spirit and sprawling sense of freedom make it a definitive work of art
In the 00s, when the Grand Theft Auto developer Rockstar Games revealed a new project, video game writers from all over the UK would make the journey to the company’s office in London. They would be ushered one by one into a darkened room to sit facing an enormous TV. There would be a dish of sweets on a low bench in front of them but, in the reverential hush that descended, it was never entirely clear if it was acceptable to eat them.
After a few moments, the screen would come to life. Rockstar would sometimes begin its presentation not with footage from its new game, but clips from classic movies. This is the context of what we are making, Rockstar was saying, and that is where we belong.

articles.description:
When our writer found himself among the hundreds on Oxford Street hoping to get their hands on early copies and collectibles, it was a heartwarming reminder of the shared experience of fandom
• The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time review – a dream come true
It is Thursday night and I am sat blurry-eyed and runny nosed outside the Argos on Oxford Street. Incredibly, I am far from alone. This is not some strange protest against the popular retailer. When the clock strikes midnight, the lavish 4K Switch 2 remake of beloved N64 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time will be released, and I have joined a lengthy queue of about 500 fans desperate to snag early copies. There are similar events taking place across the world, from Melbourne to Mexico City; at key locations, Nintendo has senior executives waiting at the tills.
These days, of course, most video games are bought as digital copies that download straight to your PC or console on the day of release. You don’t even have to get out of bed to start playing. But in a bygone era, when we used to go to shops to buy games, midnight launches offered a space for likeminded enthusiasts to gather and celebrate their fandom. Every Call of Duty, Halo or Grand Theft Auto release would have fans queueing outside branches of Game or Electronics Boutique, many dressed as favourite characters.
